1	// The pure half of the Notification Service Extension: everything that turns bytes into
2	// other bytes, with no Keychain, no CryptoKit, and no UserNotifications.
3	//
4	// It lives apart from NotificationService.swift for the same reason the wallet's Rust keeps
5	// `_impl` cores away from Tauri commands — this is the part an XCTest can drive on a
6	// simulator, and the part the Rust↔CryptoKit fixture cross-check exercises.
7	
8	import Foundation
9	
10	/// The `ezpds` object a sealed push carries beside its placeholder `aps` alert.
11	///
12	/// Wire shape (see `crates/notify-relay/src/protocol.rs`):
13	/// `{ "v": 1, "kid": 3, "enc": "<b64url>", "ct": "<b64url>" }`
14	struct NotifyEnvelope: Equatable {
15	    /// Protocol version. Only `1` is understood; anything else is a payload sealed by a
16	    /// newer instance for a newer extension, and must render as unverified rather than be
17	    /// guessed at.
18	    static let supportedVersion = 1
19	
20	    /// The `userInfo` key the sealed block travels under. Named once because it is used for two
21	    /// opposite purposes — reading the envelope, and *removing* it before delivery — and a typo
22	    /// in the second would leak ciphertext into the delivered-notification list silently.
23	    static let userInfoKey = "ezpds"
24	
25	    let version: Int
26	    /// The instance-scoped sender-key id. Not a global identifier: two Custos instances both
27	    /// start their `kid` sequence at 1, which is why the pin store is keyed by host and every
28	    /// candidate under this id is tried.
29	    let kid: Int
30	    /// HPKE encapsulated key — 65 raw bytes for DHKEM(P-256).
31	    let enc: Data
32	    /// AEAD ciphertext with the 16-byte AES-GCM tag appended.
33	    let ct: Data
34	
35	    /// Read the envelope out of an APNs `userInfo` dictionary.
36	    ///
37	    /// Returns `nil` for anything that is not a well-formed v1 envelope — a junk push from a
38	    /// misbehaving relay, a `content-available` ping, or a future version. The caller renders
39	    /// all of those identically (the unverified notice), so this deliberately does not
40	    /// distinguish "absent" from "malformed": neither is content this device can vouch for.
41	    static func parse(userInfo: [AnyHashable: Any]) -> NotifyEnvelope? {
42	        guard let block = userInfo[userInfoKey] as? [String: Any],
43	              let version = block["v"] as? Int,
44	              version == supportedVersion,
45	              let kid = block["kid"] as? Int,
46	              let encText = block["enc"] as? String,
47	              let ctText = block["ct"] as? String,
48	              let enc = Data(base64URLEncoded: encText),
49	              let ct = Data(base64URLEncoded: ctText),
50	              !enc.isEmpty, !ct.isEmpty
51	        else { return nil }
52	
53	        return NotifyEnvelope(version: version, kid: kid, enc: enc, ct: ct)
54	    }
55	}
56	
57	/// The decrypted plaintext a Custos instance seals.
58	///
59	/// Wire shape: `{ "type": …, "title": …, "body": …, "data": { … }, "pad": "…" }`. `pad` is
60	/// dropped on the floor here — its whole job was to make the *serialized APNs request* land
61	/// on a padding bucket, which is finished by the time these bytes exist. `data` is decoded
62	/// only for the small allowlist of routing fields below; everything else in it is ignored.
63	struct NotifyPayload: Equatable, Decodable {
64	    let type: String
65	    let title: String
66	    let body: String
67	    /// Structured routing data the sealing instance attached (a request id, a subject DID).
68	    /// Optional and tolerant: a payload without it — or with fields this build doesn't know —
69	    /// still renders; only the recognized identifiers survive into the delivered notification.
70	    let data: NotifyRouteData?
71	
72	    private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
73	        case type, title, body, data
74	    }
75	
76	    /// Decode sealed plaintext, rejecting a payload with nothing to render.
77	    ///
78	    /// An empty title *and* body would produce a banner indistinguishable from a silent
79	    /// delivery failure, so it is treated as a malformed payload and rendered as the
80	    /// unverified notice instead — the extension's one rule is that it never shows something
81	    /// it cannot stand behind. A `data` block that fails to decode as the routing shape is
82	    /// dropped (the banner still renders); it never fails the whole payload.
83	    static func decode(_ plaintext: Data) -> NotifyPayload? {
84	        guard let payload = try? JSONDecoder().decode(NotifyPayload.self, from: plaintext),
85	              !(payload.title.isEmpty && payload.body.isEmpty)
86	        else { return nil }
87	        return payload
88	    }
89	}
90	
91	/// The routing identifiers a verified payload may carry in `data`.
92	///
93	/// A deliberate allowlist rather than a passthrough: only these fields ever reach the
94	/// delivered notification's `userInfo`, so the app can never be steered by a field the
95	/// extension didn't decide to forward.
96	struct NotifyRouteData: Equatable, Decodable {
97	    /// A pending OAuth consent request id (`login-approval`).
98	    let requestId: String?
99	    /// The account DID the notification concerns, so a multi-identity wallet opens the
100	    /// right one.
101	    let did: String?
102	
103	    private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
104	        case requestId, did
105	    }
106	
107	    init(requestId: String?, did: String?) {
108	        self.requestId = requestId
109	        self.did = did
110	    }
111	
112	    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
113	        // Tolerant field-by-field decode: a `data` block whose recognized fields have
114	        // unexpected types reads as absent fields, never a decode failure that would take
115	        // the whole (already authenticated) payload down with it.
116	        let container = try? decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
117	        requestId = container.flatMap { try? $0.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .requestId) } ?? nil
118	        did = container.flatMap { try? $0.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .did) } ?? nil
119	    }
120	}
121	
122	/// The routing block a verified payload leaves in the delivered notification.
123	enum NotifyRoute {
124	    /// The `userInfo` key the app reads on a notification tap. Distinct from
125	    /// `NotifyEnvelope.userInfoKey` (`ezpds`, the sealed block, which is always stripped):
126	    /// this one is *written* by the extension, and only ever after HPKE Auth verified the
127	    /// payload — so its presence is itself the "this came from your instance" statement.
128	    static let userInfoKey = "ezpdsRoute"
129	
130	    /// What a rendered payload contributes to the delivered notification's `userInfo`, or
131	    /// `nil` when it carries nothing to route on. Pure so the tests can pin the contract:
132	    /// only allowlisted identifiers, plus the payload `type` the app dispatches on.
133	    static func userInfo(for payload: NotifyPayload) -> [String: String]? {
134	        var route: [String: String] = [:]
135	        if let requestId = payload.data?.requestId { route["requestId"] = requestId }
136	        if let did = payload.data?.did { route["did"] = did }
137	        guard !route.isEmpty else { return nil }
138	        route["type"] = payload.type
139	        return route
140	    }
141	}
142	
143	// MARK: - base64url
144	
145	extension Data {
146	    /// Decode unpadded base64url — the encoding every binary field in the envelope uses
147	    /// (`URL_SAFE_NO_PAD` on the Rust side). Foundation only speaks standard base64 with
148	    /// padding, so translate the alphabet and re-pad.
149	    init?(base64URLEncoded input: String) {
150	        var text = input.replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "+")
151	            .replacingOccurrences(of: "_", with: "/")
152	        let remainder = text.count % 4
153	        if remainder == 1 {
154	            // 4n+1 is not a length any base64 encoding can produce; padding it would
155	            // manufacture a decodable string out of corrupt input.
156	            return nil
157	        }
158	        if remainder > 0 {
159	            text += String(repeating: "=", count: 4 - remainder)
160	        }
161	        guard let decoded = Data(base64Encoded: text) else { return nil }
162	        self = decoded
163	    }
164	}
165	
166	// MARK: - did:key
167	
168	/// Decode a P-256 `did:key` into its raw SEC1 public-key bytes.
169	///
170	/// The pinned sender keys arrive from Custos as `did:key:z…` strings and are stored verbatim
171	/// by the wallet (`notifications.rs`), so the extension has to undo the encoding itself:
172	/// multibase base58btc (`z` prefix) wrapping the multicodec varint `0x1200` — written
173	/// little-endian-base128 as `0x80 0x24` — followed by a 33-byte compressed point.
174	///
175	/// Returns `nil` for anything that is not exactly that. A sender key this device cannot
176	/// decode is simply not a candidate; HPKE Auth mode would fail closed on it anyway, so
177	/// skipping costs nothing and misreading could not gain anything.
178	enum DidKey {
179	    /// The multicodec prefix for `p256-pub`, varint-encoded.
180	    static let p256Prefix: [UInt8] = [0x80, 0x24]
181	    /// A compressed SEC1 P-256 point: 1 tag byte + 32-byte X.
182	    static let compressedPointLength = 33
183	
184	    static func p256PublicKeyBytes(from didKey: String) -> Data? {
185	        guard didKey.hasPrefix("did:key:z") else { return nil }
186	        let multibase = String(didKey.dropFirst("did:key:z".count))
187	        guard let decoded = Base58.decode(multibase),
188	              decoded.count == p256Prefix.count + compressedPointLength,
189	              Array(decoded.prefix(p256Prefix.count)) == p256Prefix
190	        else { return nil }
191	        return Data(decoded.dropFirst(p256Prefix.count))
192	    }
193	}
194	
195	/// base58btc, the one multibase alphabet `did:key` uses.
196	///
197	/// Hand-rolled because the extension links nothing but system frameworks: a Swift package
198	/// dependency in an NSE is a second supply chain in the one target that runs on a locked
199	/// screen, for ~30 lines of long division.
200	enum Base58 {
201	    private static let alphabet = Array("REDACTED".utf8)
202	
203	    static func decode(_ input: String) -> [UInt8]? {
204	        var bytes: [UInt8] = [0]
205	        for character in input.utf8 {
206	            guard let value = alphabet.firstIndex(of: character) else { return nil }
207	            var carry = value
208	            for index in bytes.indices.reversed() {
209	                carry += 58 * Int(bytes[index])
210	                bytes[index] = UInt8(carry & 0xff)
211	                carry >>= 8
212	            }
213	            while carry > 0 {
214	                bytes.insert(UInt8(carry & 0xff), at: 0)
215	                carry >>= 8
216	            }
217	        }
218	        // Every leading '1' encodes one leading zero byte, which the arithmetic above cannot
219	        // recover (it carries no magnitude).
220	        var leadingZeros = 0
221	        for character in input.utf8 {
222	            guard character == alphabet[0] else { break }
223	            leadingZeros += 1
224	        }
225	        // Drop the seed byte and any zeros the long division introduced, then restore the
226	        // encoded ones.
227	        let significant = Array(bytes.drop(while: { $0 == 0 }))
228	        return Array(repeating: 0, count: leadingZeros) + significant
229	    }
230	}

I'm thinking through how to test the breadcrumb-recording behavior in the timeout method, but it's tricky since NotificationService requires private setters and needs to be initialized through didReceive first, which limits what I can directly test. Ah, I see — `finish()` is called before the contentHandler in `didReceive`, and since `bestAttempt` is a reference to the same `content` object, the envelope key gets stripped from `bestAttempt`'s userInfo before `didReceive` returns. So if `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire` is called after `didReceive` completes normally, it won't find the envelope key and would skip the unverified block entirely, calling `finish()` again (which is now a no-op) and invoking `contentHandler` a second time — though that double-call is an existing race condition unrelated to this issue.

The real problem is that `didReceive` is entirely synchronous with no async I/O, so it always completes within the same call stack, meaning `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire` would only fire in production if `didReceive` genuinely hangs — but even the Keychain reads are synchronous SecItem calls, though they could potentially block if the device is under load or the disk is slow.

Since the implementation is fully synchronous, the race condition between `bestAttempt` being set and `resolve()` returning can't naturally interleave without threading. To make this testable, I'd extract a pure helper function that determines whether a timed-out resolution should be recorded as a failure and what key ID to use, allowing the interlock logic to be exercised independently.

content.content:
1	// The Notification Service Extension: the only place a sealed push is ever plaintext.
2	//
3	// A Custos instance HPKE-seals a notification to this device's key and hands it to a relay
4	// that holds the APNs key but no decryption key. The relay and Apple both carry the payload
5	// as opaque bytes beside a placeholder alert ("Custos / Encrypted notification"), and
6	// `mutable-content: 1` routes it here for the ~30 seconds iOS allows before it gives up and
7	// shows the placeholder.
8	//
9	// # The constraint that shapes everything below
10	//
11	// **An NSE cannot suppress an alert push.** If this code fails, times out, or declines to
12	// attach content, iOS displays the original payload anyway. So "drop what we cannot verify"
13	// is not on the menu; the only thing under this extension's control is *what the user reads*.
14	// The rule is therefore absolute: content that opened under HPKE Auth mode renders as
15	// content, and everything else renders as the explicit unverified notice. Never a guess,
16	// never a partial render, never the placeholder passed through as though it were news.
17	//
18	// That is what keeps a relay's junk push from being an impersonation. The relay can always
19	// generate noise — it holds the APNs key — but noise arrives labelled as unverifiable, which
20	// is detectable spam and grounds for switching relays, not a forged message from your server.
21	
22	import UserNotifications
23	
24	/// The decision the extension makes about one payload, split out from the `UNNotification`
25	/// machinery so every branch is reachable from a test.
26	enum NotifyOutcome: Equatable {
27	    case rendered(NotifyPayload)
28	    case unverified(NotifyFailureReason, kid: Int?)
29	}
30	
31	enum NotifyResolver {
32	    /// The user-visible copy for a payload this device cannot vouch for.
33	    ///
34	    /// Deliberately says what happened and nothing more. It names no sender ("from your
35	    /// Custos instance" is a category, not a claim about which one), states no cause the
36	    /// extension cannot know, and offers no action — the actionable version of this lives in
37	    /// Settings, where the breadcrumbs can say whether it happened once or twenty times.
38	    static let unverifiedTitle = "Unverified notification"
39	    static let unverifiedBody = "Couldn't verify a notification from your Custos instance."
40	
41	    /// Resolve an APNs `userInfo` into what should be shown.
42	    ///
43	    /// Pure over its inputs — the Keychain reads happen in the caller — so the whole failure
44	    /// ladder is exercisable on a simulator with no push and no registered key.
45	    static func resolve(
46	        userInfo: [AnyHashable: Any],
47	        recipientPrivateKey: Data?,
48	        pins: PinnedSenderKeys
49	    ) -> NotifyOutcome {
50	        guard let envelope = NotifyEnvelope.parse(userInfo: userInfo) else {
51	            return .unverified(.malformedPayload, kid: nil)
52	        }
53	        guard let recipientPrivateKey else {
54	            return .unverified(.keysUnavailable, kid: envelope.kid)
55	        }
56	
57	        let candidates = pins.candidates(for: envelope.kid)
58	        guard !candidates.isEmpty else {
59	            return .unverified(.unknownKid, kid: envelope.kid)
60	        }
61	
62	        // Try every key pinned under this `kid`. See `PinnedSenderKeys.candidates` for why
63	        // there can be more than one; Auth mode makes a wrong guess free.
64	        for didKey in candidates {
65	            guard let senderBytes = DidKey.p256PublicKeyBytes(from: didKey) else { continue }
66	            guard let plaintext = NotifyCrypto.open(
67	                recipientPrivateKey: recipientPrivateKey,
68	                senderPublicKey: senderBytes,
69	                encapsulatedKey: envelope.enc,
70	                ciphertext: envelope.ct
71	            ) else { continue }
72	
73	            // Past this point the payload is authenticated: only a holder of a pinned sender
74	            // private key could have produced it. A body we cannot parse is therefore our own
75	            // bug or a version skew, not an attack — but it still cannot be rendered as
76	            // content, because there is no content to render.
77	            guard let payload = NotifyPayload.decode(plaintext) else {
78	                return .unverified(.malformedPlaintext, kid: envelope.kid)
79	            }
80	            return .rendered(payload)
81	        }
82	
83	        return .unverified(.openFailed, kid: envelope.kid)
84	    }
85	}
86	
87	/// What `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire` should do about a `bestAttempt` it was handed.
88	enum NotifyTimeoutOutcome: Equatable {
89	    /// `didReceive` had not finished — render the notice and record why.
90	    case cutShort(kid: Int?)
91	    /// `didReceive` already ran to completion (rendered or already-recorded-unverified) before
92	    /// the timeout fired; there is nothing left to do.
93	    case alreadyResolved
94	}
95	
96	enum NotifyTimeout {
97	    /// Decide what a timeout means for one `bestAttempt`, split out from
98	    /// `UNNotificationServiceExtension` for the same reason `NotifyResolver.resolve` is: so the
99	    /// interlock between `didReceive` stripping the sealed block and a timeout racing it is
100	    /// exercisable from a test without threads or a real 30-second wait.
101	    ///
102	    /// Pure over `userInfo`: the presence of the sealed block IS the "we never finished" signal
103	    /// — `didReceive`'s `finish()` strips it and writes the notice in the same breath, so it can
104	    /// only still be present here if resolution was cut short. Testing that rather than the
105	    /// title keeps the two facts from drifting.
106	    static func evaluate(userInfo: [AnyHashable: Any]) -> NotifyTimeoutOutcome {
107	        guard userInfo[NotifyEnvelope.userInfoKey] != nil else { return .alreadyResolved }
108	        // `kid` comes along when the envelope parsed far enough to have one, same as every other
109	        // breadcrumb `NotifyResolver.resolve` records — a key-desync signature arriving via the
110	        // timeout path is still worth showing.
111	        return .cutShort(kid: NotifyEnvelope.parse(userInfo: userInfo)?.kid)
112	    }
113	}
114	
115	final class NotificationService: UNNotificationServiceExtension {
116	    private var contentHandler: ((UNNotificationContent) -> Void)?
117	    private var bestAttempt: UNMutableNotificationContent?
118	
119	    override func didReceive(
120	        _ request: UNNotificationRequest,
121	        withContentHandler contentHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationContent) -> Void
122	    ) {
123	        self.contentHandler = contentHandler
124	        guard let content = request.content.mutableCopy() as? UNMutableNotificationContent else {
125	            // `UNNotificationContent.mutableCopy()` is documented to return the mutable class, so
126	            // this is a platform-contract violation rather than a state a payload can produce.
127	            // It still cannot be allowed to deliver `request.content`: that content is immutable,
128	            // so the sealed block cannot be stripped from it, and its title/body are the relay's
129	            // placeholder — the one combination the extension's rule forbids. A fresh content
130	            // carrying only the notice is the sole way to honour both halves here.
131	            //
132	            // No breadcrumb: the failure vocabulary describes payloads, and reporting this as a
133	            // payload problem would send the user looking at their keys for a bug in ours.
134	            contentHandler(Self.unverifiedContent())
135	            return
136	        }
137	        bestAttempt = content
138	
139	        let outcome = NotifyResolver.resolve(
140	            userInfo: request.content.userInfo,
141	            recipientPrivateKey: NotifyKeychain.read(
142	                account: NotifyKeychain.notificationKeyAccount
143	            ),
144	            pins: PinnedSenderKeys.parse(
145	                NotifyKeychain.read(account: NotifyKeychain.pinnedSenderKeysAccount)
146	            )
147	        )
148	
149	        switch outcome {
150	        case let .rendered(payload):
151	            content.title = payload.title
152	            content.body = payload.body
153	            // Routing survives ONLY on the verified path: `ezpdsRoute`'s presence in a
154	            // delivered notification is the statement that HPKE Auth vouched for it, which
155	            // is what lets the app deep-link on a tap without re-deciding trust.
156	            if let route = NotifyRoute.userInfo(for: payload) {
157	                content.userInfo[NotifyRoute.userInfoKey] = route
158	            }
159	        case let .unverified(reason, kid):
160	            content.title = NotifyResolver.unverifiedTitle
161	            content.body = NotifyResolver.unverifiedBody
162	            NotifyBreadcrumbs.record(reason, kid: kid)
163	        }
164	
165	        Self.finish(content)
166	        contentHandler(content)
167	    }
168	
169	    /// iOS is about to give up on us.
170	    ///
171	    /// Whatever is in `bestAttempt` is delivered, so this path has to satisfy the same three
172	    /// obligations `didReceive` does — say "unverified" rather than let the relay's placeholder
173	    /// stand in for the server's words, strip the sealed block, and record why. None gets an
174	    /// exception for running late: a timeout is the one route by which unstripped ciphertext,
175	    /// under a title the user reads as authentic, could reach the delivered-notification list —
176	    /// and a timeout that skipped the breadcrumb is the one route by which Settings could report
177	    /// a clean bill of health while the banner says otherwise.
178	    override func serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire() {
179	        guard let contentHandler, let bestAttempt else { return }
180	        if case let .cutShort(kid) = NotifyTimeout.evaluate(userInfo: bestAttempt.userInfo) {
181	            bestAttempt.title = NotifyResolver.unverifiedTitle
182	            bestAttempt.body = NotifyResolver.unverifiedBody
183	            NotifyBreadcrumbs.record(.timedOut, kid: kid)
184	        }
185	        Self.finish(bestAttempt)
186	        contentHandler(bestAttempt)
187	    }
188	
189	    /// The last thing done to any content that leaves this extension.
190	    ///
191	    /// The sealed block has served its purpose and must not ride along into the delivered
192	    /// notification, where the app — and anything reading `UNUserNotificationCenter`'s delivered
193	    /// list — would see ciphertext it has no use for. Factored out because "every exit path"
194	    /// is the actual requirement, and inlining it at each one is how an exit path gets missed.
195	    private static func finish(_ content: UNMutableNotificationContent) {
196	        content.userInfo.removeValue(forKey: NotifyEnvelope.userInfoKey)
197	    }
198	
199	    /// A fresh content carrying nothing but the unverified notice.
200	    ///
201	    /// For the exit where no mutable copy exists to strip, so substituting content is the only
202	    /// way to avoid delivering the sealed block.
203	    private static func unverifiedContent() -> UNMutableNotificationContent {
204	        let content = UNMutableNotificationContent()
205	        content.title = NotifyResolver.unverifiedTitle
206	        content.body = NotifyResolver.unverifiedBody
207	        return content
208	    }
209	}

# Changelog fragments

Every pull request that changes a shipped surface must add a short Markdown fragment:

```text
changelog.d/<id>.<type>.md
```

- `<id>` is the Linear issue identifier in lowercase (for example, `mm-358`). If a
  change has no Linear issue, use the pull request number (for example, `271`).
- `<type>` is one of `added`, `changed`, `fixed`, `removed`, or `security`.
- The file contains one concise, user- or operator-facing Markdown statement. Do not
  include a heading or bullet marker; the release script supplies both.
- Use more than one fragment when a change belongs in more than one category.

Example (`changelog.d/mm-358.added.md`):

```markdown
Release notes now collect user-visible changes from pull requests automatically.
```

The CI gate requires a fragment when a pull request changes a deployable surface:

- server or shared runtime source under `crates/*/src/`, plus PDS runtime assets;
- either mobile app's frontend, native runtime source, static assets, or Tauri config;
- the public marketing site;
- the deployed MCP surfaces — the stdio Custos MCP server (`tools/mcp/src/`) and the
  credential-forwarding sidecar (`tools/mcp-sidecar/src/`, plus its image/config), which
  ships as a Railway service and re-exports the stdio server's tool surface;
- the notification relay's own image, entrypoint, and Railway config
  (`crates/notify-relay/`), which ships as a separate service;
- workspace runtime dependency manifests, the production image/config, or the NixOS
  runtime module.

Documentation, tests, design files, CI configuration, scripts, developer tooling, and
other repository-internal changes do not trigger the presence requirement. Any fragment
that is present is still checked for a valid name and non-empty content.

The browser test harness (`apps/*/src/lib/harness/`) is developer tooling despite its
path: it is double-gated on `import.meta.env.DEV && VITE_HARNESS` and proven absent from
production builds by `pnpm check:harness-absence`, so the gate skips it explicitly rather
than letting the broad `apps/*/src/` rule claim it.

`just set-version X.Y.Z` groups all fragments into a dated Keep a Changelog release
section in `CHANGELOG.md`, then deletes the consumed fragments. This README remains.

1	# Shared iOS Swift sources
2	
3	Last verified: 2026-07-29
4	
5	## Purpose
6	
7	Swift that belongs to the iOS apps but to neither app's Rust crate. Today that is exactly one
8	thing: the wallet's **Notification Service Extension**, which unseals encrypted push
9	notifications on arrival.
10	
11	It sits at the repo root rather than under `apps/identity-wallet/` for the same reason
12	`scripts/ios/` does — the XcodeGen template that compiles it is shared by both apps, so its
13	inputs are shared too. The operator console will grow an extension from these same sources when it
14	adopts notifications.
15	
16	## Contracts
17	
18	### `NotificationService/` — the extension (`{{app.name}}_NSE`)
19	
20	**Exposes:** `NotificationService`, a `UNNotificationServiceExtension` subclass iOS
21	instantiates via `NSExtensionPrincipalClass` when a push carries `mutable-content: 1`.
22

24	- A payload that opens under HPKE Auth mode renders as content. **Everything else renders as

# Shared iOS Swift sources

Last verified: 2026-07-29

## Purpose

Swift that belongs to the iOS apps but to neither app's Rust crate. Today that is exactly one
thing: the wallet's **Notification Service Extension**, which unseals encrypted push
notifications on arrival.

It sits at the repo root rather than under `apps/identity-wallet/` for the same reason
`scripts/ios/` does — the XcodeGen template that compiles it is shared by both apps, so its
inputs are shared too. The operator console will grow an extension from these same sources when it
adopts notifications.

## Contracts

### `NotificationService/` — the extension (`{{app.name}}_NSE`)

**Exposes:** `NotificationService`, a `UNNotificationServiceExtension` subclass iOS
instantiates via `NSExtensionPrincipalClass` when a push carries `mutable-content: 1`.

**Guarantees:**
- A payload that opens under HPKE Auth mode renders as content. **Everything else renders as
  the explicit unverified notice** — never a guess, never a partial render, never the relay's
  placeholder passed through as though it were news. This is the extension's single rule, and
  it holds on the timeout path too (`serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire`).
- The sealed `ezpds` block is stripped from the delivered notification, so ciphertext never
  reaches the app's delivered-notification list.
- A **verified** payload's routing identifiers survive into the delivered notification as the
  `ezpdsRoute` `userInfo` block (`{type, requestId?, did?}` — an allowlist read from the
  payload's `data`, never a passthrough). It is written only on the rendered path, so its
  presence in a delivered notification is itself the "HPKE Auth vouched for this" statement the
  app's tap handler relies on to deep-link (the wallet still re-fetches everything it displays
  from the server by `requestId`). An unverified or timed-out delivery never carries it.
- Every failure leaves a breadcrumb in the shared Keychain, best effort. A Keychain that will
  not take a diagnostic never costs the user the notice itself.

**Expects:**
- `keychain-access-groups` listing `$(AppIdentifierPrefix)org.obsign.shared` **first**
  (`apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/Entitlements.NSE.plist`). Nothing here names an access group
  in a query — naming one would mean discovering `AppIdentifierPrefix` at runtime, on the one
  code path that must work on a locked screen — so the entitlement's *order* is the mechanism.
- The wallet having registered: `notification-key-priv` and `notification-sender-keys`, both
  under `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock`, written by `notifications.rs`.
- iOS 17. `HPKE.Recipient`'s auth-mode initializer does not exist before it.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `NotificationService.swift` | The `UNNotificationServiceExtension` shell, plus `NotifyResolver` — the pure failure ladder every branch of which is a banner someone reads |
| `NotifyCrypto.swift` | CryptoKit `HPKE.Recipient` in auth mode, suite/`info`/`aad` pinned to `crates/crypto/src/hpke.rs` |
| `NotifyEnvelope.swift` | Envelope + payload parsing, base64url, `did:key` → SEC1, base58 |
| `NotifyKeychain.swift` | The shared-Keychain reads, and the pin document's shape |
| `NotifyBreadcrumbs.swift` | The bounded failure log the app surfaces in Settings |

### `NotificationServiceTests/` — the logic-test bundle (`{{app.name}}_NSETests`)

Compiled with the extension's sources rather than linking them: an app extension has no
testable module to import, since there is no `TEST_HOST` an extension can be loaded into.

`NotifyFixtureTests` is the **cross-implementation check** — it opens
`crates/crypto/tests/fixtures/notify/hpke-notify-v1.json` (sealed by Rust's `hpke` crate) with
CryptoKit. RFC 9180's appendix carries no vector for this suite, so nothing else proves the two
agree on the pinned suite, the `info` string, the empty `aad`, and the key encodings. The
fixture is referenced **in place** by the template — there is no copy here to drift.

## Dependencies

System frameworks only: CryptoKit, Foundation, Security, UserNotifications. Deliberately no
Swift package dependency — a package in the extension is a second supply chain in the one
process that runs on a locked screen.

## Key Decisions

- **Swift, not a second Rust staticlib.** Decryption is ~200 lines of CryptoKit; a second
  staticlib would double the iOS build's slowest step for it.
- **Breadcrumbs go to the shared Keychain, not an app-group container.** The keychain group is
  already entitled and needs no Apple Developer portal work; an app group would be a second new
  entitlement on both bundles. The cost is that a push arriving before the first unlock after a
  reboot leaves no breadcrumb — the one failure that repairs itself, and the least worth
  recording.
- **The extension is gated to the wallet's bundle id** in `scripts/ios/project.yml`. An app
  extension is a separate bundle needing its own App ID, profile, and signing secret; rendering
  one for admin-companion would cost a second set of those for an extension that cannot decrypt
  anything until the console has a shared keychain group and registered notification keys of its own.

## Invariants

- The Keychain service name, account names, and both JSON document shapes in
  `NotifyKeychain.swift` / `NotifyBreadcrumbs.swift` are **copies** of constants in
  `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/{keychain,notifications}.rs`. Two separate bundles can
  only agree by both spelling the same strings; a rename on one side is silent on the other.
- `PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME` is pinned to `NotificationService` in the template. It is half of
  `NSExtensionPrincipalClass`, so a drift leaves iOS unable to instantiate the extension — a
  failure indistinguishable from a push that never arrived. `just ios-check` greps the pbxproj
  for it.
- The failure `reason` vocabulary (`NotifyFailureReason`) is shared with the app's
  `NotificationFailure.reason` and the frontend's `NotificationFailureReason`. Both readers
  tolerate an unrecognized value on purpose: the extension versions independently, and the entry
  a strict reader would drop is the one the user is asking about. A new case still needs wording
  in `apps/identity-wallet/src/lib/notification-health.ts`.
- CI gates, in order of what they can catch:
  - `just _nse-typecheck` (macOS, part of `just ios-pr-check`) — `swiftc -typecheck` of the
    extension's sources, then of the test bundle exactly as the template composes it, against
    the real iOS SDK at the deployment target both apps declare. No simulator, no signing, no
    generated Xcode project. This is the only thing that compiles this Swift before a release
    archive would.
  - `just ios-template-check` (Linux) — target present, gated to the wallet, embedded,
    principal class and module name, entitlements order and least privilege, sources exist.
  - `just ios-check` (macOS) — the same structural facts in the generated pbxproj.
  Nothing *runs* the tests in CI: `ios-pr-check` performs no `xcodebuild`, so the fixture
  cross-check is a local `xcodebuild test -scheme <app>_NSETests` (or `⌘U` on that scheme).

[ -d "$appex" ] || continue
      check "$appex" "PlugIns/$(basename "$appex")"
    done

    [ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || { echo "✗ $(basename "$ipa") is not shippable — see above" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "✓ $(basename "$ipa") signing verified"

# Typecheck the Notification Service Extension's Swift against the real iOS SDK — the
# extension's sources alone, then the test bundle exactly as the XcodeGen template composes
# it (extension sources compiled INTO the test target, since an app extension has no module
# to import).
#
# This exists because no other lane compiles Swift at all: `_pr-check` cross-compiles the
# Rust staticlib and stops, and the archive that would surface a Swift error only runs on
# push to main, holding signing secrets. Without this, a compile error in ~800 lines of
# security-critical Swift reaches TestFlight before anything objects — and the
# file-existence loop in ios-template-check would have to stand in for a compiler.
#
# `-typecheck`, not a build: it needs no simulator, no signing, and no generated Xcode
# project, so it runs on a bare checkout in seconds. macOS-only (xcrun); the caller is the
# macOS pr-check.
_nse-typecheck:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    sdk="$(xcrun --sdk iphonesimulator --show-sdk-path)"
    platform="$(xcrun --sdk iphonesimulator --show-sdk-platform-path)"
    # The deployment target is pinned to the same 17.0 both apps declare: CryptoKit's HPKE
    # auth-mode initializer does not exist before it, so a lower target here would let a
    # regression that raises the real minimum pass unnoticed.
    common=(-typecheck -sdk "$sdk" -target arm64-apple-ios17.0-simulator)
    xcrun swiftc "${common[@]}" ios/NotificationService/*.swift
    echo "✓ NSE sources typecheck"
    # XCTest's Swift overlay lives beside the framework, not inside it; without the -I the
    # C macros are found instead and every assertion reads as an unknown identifier.
    xcrun swiftc "${common[@]}" \
      -F "$platform/Developer/Library/Frameworks" \
      -I "$platform/Developer/usr/lib" \
      ios/NotificationService/*.swift ios/NotificationServiceTests/*.swift
    echo "✓ NSE test bundle typechecks"

# Compile the app's Icon Composer document (AppIcon.icon, referenced in place by
# the scripts/ios/project.yml template) with actool — the same compiler Xcode's
# build invokes — so a malformed icon.json or a layer SVG the Apple toolchain
# can't parse fails the PR gate instead of the post-merge TestFlight archive.
# macOS-only (xcrun); the callers are the macOS pr-check recipes. actool's exit
# code alone is not trustworthy, so the recipe also requires an Assets.car and
# greps the tool output for errors. A MISSING bundle fails too: both apps ship
# one, so absence in this gate means a miswired path, not an icon-less app.
_icon-compile app_dir:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    icon="{{app_dir}}/AppIcon.icon"
    if [ ! -d "$icon" ]; then
      echo "✗ missing AppIcon.icon in {{app_dir}} — both apps ship one; a missing bundle here means a miswired path" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    out="$(mktemp -d)"
    log="$(xcrun actool "$icon" --compile "$out" \
      --platform iphoneos --minimum-deployment-target 14.0 \
      --app-icon AppIcon --output-partial-info-plist "$out/AppIcon-partial.plist" \
      --output-format human-readable-text --notices --warnings 2>&1)" || { echo "$log" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "$log"
    if echo "$log" | grep -qi ': error:'; then
      echo "✗ actool reported errors compiling $icon" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ ! -f "$out/Assets.car" ]; then
      echo "✗ actool produced no Assets.car from $icon" >&2
      exit 1
    fi

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
1. **Extracting the pure decision, not just adding a call.** The obvious fix was one line — call `NotifyBreadcrumbs.record` inside the existing `if` in `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire`. But this codebase has a strong, explicit convention (see `NotifyResolver.resolve`'s doc comment) of splitting *decisions* out from `UNNotificationServiceExtension` override methods, specifically because Apple's extension lifecycle methods can't be invoked standalone in a test — there's no way to construct a `NotificationService`, feed it a request, and then fire a timeout on it independently. By extracting `NotifyTimeout.evaluate(userInfo:)` as a free function over plain data, the exact race this bug lived in (timeout firing before `didReceive` finishes) became a two-line assertion instead of an untestable code path.

2. **Three-tier "shared vocabulary" with no compiler to enforce it.** `NotifyFailureReason` exists in three unrelated forms — a Swift `enum` with real cases, a Rust `String` field with a doc-comment listing valid values, and a TypeScript union with an open `(string & {})` escape hatch for forward-compatibility. None of these types actually constrain each other; the contract is entirely social (a doc-comment discipline: "a new case here needs one there"). This is a deliberate trade-off given the NSE and the app ship as separate bundles that can be at different versions in production simultaneously — a strict shared type would be a lie.

3. **Verifying Swift without a full iOS build.** `swiftc -typecheck` against the plain macOS SDK resolved production code fine but failed on `XCTest` symbol lookup — the Swift *overlay* for XCTest lives beside the framework binary, not inside it, so it needs an explicit `-I` search path into the platform's `usr/lib`. The repo already had this solved as `just _nse-typecheck`, which types-checks against the `iphonesimulator` SDK instead of `macosx` — the same commands CI's `ios-pr-check` runs, so I could get real confidence without generating an Xcode project or touching a simulator.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Summary

Fixed [MM-493](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-493/nse-timeout-path-renders-the-unverified-notice-without-recording-a): the NSE's timeout path now records a `.timedOut` breadcrumb before substituting the unverified notice, closing the gap where Settings could report "green" while every push banner said "couldn't verify."

- [NotificationService.swift](ios/NotificationService/NotificationService.swift) — extracted the timeout decision into a pure, testable `NotifyTimeout.evaluate(userInfo:)`, and `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire` now calls `NotifyBreadcrumbs.record(.timedOut, kid:)` when resolution was cut short.
- [NotifyBreadcrumbs.swift](ios/NotificationService/NotifyBreadcrumbs.swift) — added the `.timedOut` / `TIMED_OUT` case to the shared reason vocabulary.
- [notifications.rs](apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/notifications.rs), [ipc/notifications.ts](apps/identity-wallet/src/lib/ipc/notifications.ts), [notification-health.ts](apps/identity-wallet/src/lib/notification-health.ts) — mirrored the new reason across the Rust doc comment, the TS union, and Settings' wording (`info` severity, no advice — a timeout is self-resolving and names no fix, same as `KEYS_UNAVAILABLE`).
- Added Swift tests for the new pure function and a Vitest case for the new wording; new [changelog fragment](changelog.d/mm-493.fixed.md).

**Verified:** `pnpm vitest run` (11/11 pass), `pnpm check` (0 errors), `cargo fmt --check`, and `just _nse-typecheck` — the actual CI gate that compiles this Swift — all pass clean.

**Left out deliberately:** the issue's second "consider" bullet (an extension heartbeat sentinel to detect a fully broken app↔extension keychain contract) is a separate, larger design — distinguishing "extension never ran" from "extension ran but failed" needs new app-side comparison logic against `UNUserNotificationCenter`'s delivered list. I'd treat that as its own follow-up issue rather than folding it into this fix; let me know if you want me to file it or scope it now.

No commits made — say the word when you want this committed and/or a PR opened (the branch is already `claude/nse-timeout-breadcrumb-69d830`, based on current `origin/main`).
